description: N-gram extraction edge cases: NOUN+ADJ+NOUN trigram, PUNCT boundary, mixed Hebrew/Latin, lemma_phrase divergence.
notes: Wave 2 closes four gaps from C04 Wave 1: (1) NOUN+ADJ+NOUN trigram had no positive test case despite being in VALID_POS_PATTERNS; (2) PUNCT token behavior was unverified; (3) mixed-script PROPN+PROPN was untested; (4) lemma_phrase silent divergence was undetectable by set-key oracle. No implementation changes — all gaps were gold/test coverage gaps.

cases.description: NOUN+ADJ+NOUN trigram — מרכז רפואי עיר (regional medical center); 3-token sentence yields 2 bigrams + 1 trigram
cases.notes: Proves NOUN+ADJ+NOUN is in VALID_POS_PATTERNS and the sliding window produces all 3 sub-spans (NOUN+ADJ bigram at positions 0-1, ADJ+NOUN bigram at 1-2, NOUN+ADJ+NOUN trigram at 0-2)

cases.description: PUNCT token breaks n-gram window — comma between two NOUN groups; no bigram/trigram spans the boundary
cases.notes: PUNCT token at index 2. Windows containing PUNCT fail is_valid_pos_pattern() (NOUN+PUNCT, PUNCT+NOUN, NOUN+NOUN+PUNCT, NOUN+PUNCT+NOUN, PUNCT+NOUN+NOUN — none in VALID_POS_PATTERNS). Only the two NOUN+NOUN bigrams on each side pass. No n-gram spans the comma boundary.

cases.description: Mixed Hebrew/Latin PROPN+PROPN bigram — Apple ישראל
cases.notes: Latin token preserved as-is in surface_text and lemma_phrase. PROPN+PROPN is a valid bigram pattern. Confirms mixed-script token sequences are handled identically to pure Hebrew.

cases.description: Lemma divergence — עיתונים ישנים (plural inflected) has lemma עיתון ישן (singular base)
cases.notes: surface_text = inflected tokens joined; lemma_phrase = lemma tokens joined. Both differ here. Used by validate_ngram_lemmas() to verify that secondary oracle detects silent lemma corruption. The main set-key oracle cannot catch a regression that leaves surface_text correct but corrupts lemma_phrase.
